audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts read Skill/Skill/Skill/Graves/Skill/Graves/Graves while the whys[] beside them said the opposite on four rows ('Graves' double-dash... zone you' on a Skill row, 'Level 3 E Facebreaker gives you the pull', 'your W trades beat his reload-gated damage', 'your Grit sustain brawls through his early burst').
audit.why: The mirror (graves__sett) set the chart to the packet — Graves / Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Graves — and this brief's packet chart agrees on the rows in question.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 5 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with ratings moved to match; the whys already described these owners correctly, so only the tokens and the full-layer phase whys needed work.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike promised that R 'flips him out of position and past his dash range' without ever saying that The Show Stopper is a 400-range cast — the shortest reach of anything in the fight.
audit.why: Sett R range is 400 and its cooldown is 120/100/80s; Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s and its cooldown drops further on basic attacks. The whole level-6 window is 'can you get inside 400 while Quickdraw is down', and the page never said so.
audit.corrected: R's 400 range priced into phases[4].why and the level-6 spike, Quickdraw's 12s at rank 5 keyed to the first-item line, Facebreaker's 16s to the level-3 lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate errors. (a) 'Fortune's End' appears in spikes[0] — that ability does not exist on Graves; it is Xayah's. (b) Graves' Q is named 'Buckshot' in three places and his R is called 'End of the Line' — the names are wrong and swapped: Q is End of the Line, R is Collateral Damage. (c) The page repeatedly says 'Q slow' for Sett — Knuckle Down has no slow. (d) Facebreaker is called a pull-stun everywhere, but a lone target on one side is slowed, not stunned.
audit.why: packet.enemyAbilities and the kit file both give Q = End of the Line and R = Collateral Damage. Riot's Sett Q text is empowered attacks plus move speed, no slow. Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The mirror recorded (d) as the decisive rule in this lane.
audit.corrected: Fabricated 'Fortune's End' removed; Q and R renamed correctly in spikes[3], late and wants.foe[0]; the phantom Q slow replaced with the real instruction — pull him ACROSS your minions so Facebreaker stuns — in spikes[0], mid and phases[2].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The applicable missing interaction was absent: End of the Line detonates on terrain, so Graves can cut off a retreat from a champion who has no dash at all.
audit.why: Sett's only escape is Flash. A player who spends Flash on the damage and then walks a wall line has nothing left when the shell detonates behind him.
audit.corrected: Written into dontsFull[2] — retreat along the wall he shot, and hold Flash for the wall rather than the damage.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Graves burns Quickdraw.
edits.after: Facebreaker (16s) is online — it stuns only with a target on each side, so pull him across your minions once Quickdraw is spent.

edits.before: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier, but Graves has his core tools too. Keep the grit bar honest: trade in, W-shield his return damage, out.
edits.after: Q ranks make your punch trades heavier and his reloads gate his damage. Punish a reload: punch in, cash W dead-centre, step out before Quickdraw.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Graves doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: The Show Stopper reaches only 400, so close before Quickdraw resets. Land it and he cannot dash out of the carry; miss it and he kites you.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Graves. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Graves through Quickdraw (12s at rank 5). Force your trades in the window while it is down.

edits.after: Retreat along the wall he shot

edits.before: Dumping autos into Graves with an empty grit bar and no E — your W hits like a pillow and he just out-trades you on cooldowns.
edits.after: End of the Line detonates on terrain and cuts your retreat — you have no dash, so hold Flash for the wall, not for the damage.

edits.before: Once you have E Facebreaker, wait for Graves to burn his E Quickdraw dash for the Fortune's End reload, then pull him in with Q slow and W the point-blank shot he can't kite from.
edits.after: Once Facebreaker (16s) is up, wait for Graves to spend Quickdraw or drop into a reload, then pull him across your minions so it stuns instead of slowing, and cash Haymaker point-blank.

edits.before: Your R The Show Stopper flips him out of position and past his dash range — bait his Quickdraw first, then all-in while it's on cooldown to lock him into a full W.
edits.after: The Show Stopper reaches only 400, so bait Quickdraw (12s) before you step in — once the carry starts he cannot dash out, and he lands centred in your Haymaker panel.

edits.before: Graves comes back online as a lethality carry — his Q Buckshot and R End of the Line burst you before you can stick, so use minions to block spacing and dive only with a lead.
edits.after: Graves comes back online as a lethality carry — End of the Line (Q) and Collateral Damage (R) burst you before you can stick, so put minions in the way and dive only with a lead.

edits.before: Graves owns level 1 with two Quickdraw charges and buckshot burst while you have no gap-closer — respect his range, farm safely, and soak Grit rather than eating a full Q.
edits.after: Graves owns level 1 — his shotgun burst outranges you and you have no gap-closer at all. Respect the spacing, farm, and soak the chip as Grit rather than eating End of the Line.

edits.before: From 2 on the lane flips your way: your E pull and Q slow catch him once his dash is down, and Grit sustain lets your W out-trade his reload-gated damage through level 5.
edits.after: From 2 the lane flips your way: pull him across your minions so Facebreaker stuns rather than slows, and Grit lets Haymaker out-trade his reload-gated damage through level 5.

edits.before: Graves scales into a lethality threat again — his Buckshot and R burst chunk you before you commit, so block skillshots with minions and only dive when you're ahead.
edits.after: Graves scales into a lethality threat again — End of the Line and Collateral Damage chunk you before you commit, so block the skillshots with minions and dive only when ahead.

edits.before: To poke with Q Buckshot and dash away on E
edits.after: To poke with End of the Line and dash out on E

notes: Two fabricated names were on this page: 'Fortune's End' (that is Xayah's ability, not Graves') and 'Buckshot' used for his Q while 'End of the Line' was used for his R — the two real names were present but attached to the wrong slots. Both are fixed. The mirror's safety-critical finding applies here in reverse: the Graves page told its reader to E-dash out of The Show Stopper's carry, which is impossible; on this page the equivalent is now stated positively — land the 400-range cast and he cannot dash out, so the whole level-6 window is about closing to 400 while Quickdraw is down. The full layer still says 'E-stun' in tradeGood, dosFull[1] and breakdown.trading, which is only true when a second target is on the far side; that boilerplate is shared across every Sett page and needs one coordinated pass.
